author: Bobby Grayson
description: My first cut refused to fold a chain when a later value read a key an earlier link wrote (socket |> assign(:count, c) |> assign(:label, socket.assigns.count)). That refusal is unnecessary and would have been a false blocker: the intermediate socket of a chain is ANONYMOUS, so no value expression in the chain can name anything but the original socket variable, and Elixir's own %{s | ..} reads every field off that same original. The two therefore agree. The one refusal that stays is the same key written twice in one chain -- the record update has one slot per key, and dropping the first write would drop its sub-expressions with it, so anything unsupported inside them would go unreported. Fixture error_assign_chain_dup pins it.
title: Removed the over-conservative refusal in the assign chain fold
